I have $486 and no monopolies. I cannot build houses. Player 1 has almost no cash and owns a dangerous dark blue monopoly with two houses on Boardwalk.

Player 3 has $940 and owns Baltic, Ventnor, and Pacific. They have no property set. Player 4 has $1310 and is on Park Place.

Player 4 owns Oriental, Connecticut, St. James, Atlantic, and Water Works. They have no monopoly. I am still on my turn after auctioning Pacific.

Player 4 likely landed on Park Place during their previous turn and paid rent. I have no reason to mortgage any properties.

Mortgaging would cost too much in interest and reduce rent income. I am evaluating trades to complete a monopoly, but the orange set is blocked because New York Avenue is still on the bank.

I cannot complete a pink or red set yet. The bank still holds the remaining cards for both. A railroads trade would be valuable but would not create a color monopoly. Player 1 is cash poor and might want money, but giving it to them would help them build more houses.

Player 1 cannot build another house on Park Place because they only have $64. Player 4 has $1310 and wants monopolies, but I should not trade cash to player 1. I also decided not to sell Tennessee Avenue, since it blocks player 4 from completing the orange set.

I previously refused a $650 offer for St. James from player 4. That trade would give me two of three orange properties, but I lack anything they want in return.

I cannot afford to buy St. James for $300–400 because that would leave me too vulnerable to Boardwalk. No color set is fully owned by another player, so no trade can complete a monopoly.

No trade can complete a color set because the missing pieces are mostly in the bank. The light blue set is too weak to justify spending cash. I will end my turn.
